items.title: Greece v England: Women’s World Cup playoff semi-final, first leg – live
items.summary: ⚽ World Cup qualifying news, 5.30pm BST kick-off in Crete ⚽ Wiegman hails Toone | And read Moving the Goalposts Good evening from the Pankritio Stadium. We have the Sea of Crete to our left and some beautiful mountains to our right, whilst the England goalkeepers are warming up in front us as another blue-sky day turns to twilight. The scene may be pretty but the atmosphere is calm, quiet and frankly a bit flat. Tickets were free for this match but the locals don’t appear particularly enthused and it’s fair to say Women’s World Cup fever has not gripped the city of Heraklion just yet. There are a few hundred England fans here, currently outnumbering the Greeks. I can see Chelsea, Birmingham City and Derby County flags amongst the England banners draped behind the goal. Continue reading...

items.title: Manchester United’s early wobble makes Tottenham visit a must-win for Carrick
items.summary: After a scratchy start in the league, injuries and an underwhelming Rashford, Spurs’s visit to Old Trafford is already crucial for the hosts The noise in the Premier League was focused elsewhere for the last two weeks of the international break, allowing a glorious silence to drift across Manchester United. Without Manchester City’s woes, Michael Carrick may have faced a more difficult time, with plenty to review in regards to the first five games of the season. United sit solemnly in 12th with only one league win, and misery needs company. The hosts will find just that at Old Trafford on Saturday evening. Tottenham, bottom of the Premier League, visit, with both sides hoping to kickstart their season. Spurs have secured a measly two points after a summer where £300m was spent on Roberto De Zerbi’s rebuild but the architect’s drawings are already at risk of being set alight. For Carrick and United, beating the worst team in the league is close to a necessity as they enter a very difficult run of fixtures. Continue reading...

items.title: Oliver Glasner: ‘There was no plan for me to be Nottingham Forest manager’
items.summary: On Sunday, Austrian returns to Crystal Palace, the club he left in the summer after leading them to unprecedented success, but accepts there could be ‘booing’ Oliver Glasner puffs his cheeks and starts the search for the right words to explain his emotions as he prepares to return to Crystal Palace for the first time since leaving. There is the small matter of heading back on Sunday with Nottingham Forest to Selhurst Park, where bitterness runs deep over the club seizing Palace’s place in the Europa League last season. Forest’s owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Palace for defamation relating to a banner unfurled by their supporters and the rivalry heightened when Glasner joined Forest in the summer, 40 days after winning the Conference League with Palace. “I know I will be, but I don’t want to be in the middle of all the comments and the stories about this game,” he says in the boardroom at Forest’s training base. By which point Glasner, a charismatic and intelligent individual who studied for an economics degree while a player in Austria, has turned to Faust, by the German writer Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, to explain how he feels about facing his previous club. “Two hearts are beating in my chest,” he says, tapping his torso, alluding to a line in the classic play. “Here is a little bit similar, because we had a little bit more than two great years [at Palace].” Continue reading...
